summary: Stevens County, WA lookout on the Spokane Indian Reservation: first built 1932, a 78-foot tower reported in 1935, removed or destroyed in 1962; the summit now holds a communication site.

facts.design: 3-legged wooden tower with 7x7 ft cab, tent and cabin (1932); L-4 cab living quarters added 1934
facts.status_note: The lookout is gone. A communication structure stands at the summit.

access.note: Tribal land on the Spokane Indian Reservation; WillhiteWeb says access past the houses is probably allowed by old easements

visit.trail_note: Dirt road to the top, with ruts in places; the parking area is at the summit

notes_for_editor: Two accounts do not agree and the sources do not explain how. The register, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb date the first lookout to 1932. A Spokesman-Review item quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, dated August 17, 1935, reports a 78-foot tower completed that year. The federal station description quoted on the same page gives 75 feet. The record's height_m of 23.8 matches the 78-foot figure; it was left unchanged and the story gives both figures. Staffing and fires: none in the sources read. Access is recorded as permission because the site is on tribal land. The WillhiteWeb easement remark is the only access statement. Used 1 WebSearch and 4 page reads.
